rules.title: California FEHA housing discrimination: source of income and subsidized-tenant screening limits
rules.requirement: Housing owners may not discriminate against or harass a person because of source of income, which includes public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. Advertisements may not indicate a source-of-income preference. Income standards must count the aggregate income of persons residing together on the same basis as married persons. Where a government rent subsidy applies, income standards must be based on the tenant's portion of the rent. Where a subsidy applies, an applicant who is screened on credit history must be offered the option to submit lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay, given reasonable time to respond, and have that evidence reasonably considered in lieu of credit history. Owners may still ask about the level or source of income, verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity.

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of any housing accommodation. The text states no unit-count, age or owner-occupancy exemptions. The credit-history alternative-evidence duty applies only where there is a government rent subsidy.
coverage.other_conditions: The credit-history and tenant-portion income-standard rules apply only in instances of a government rent subsidy.

rules.exemptions: Not discrimination to make a written or oral inquiry about the level or source of income (subd. (p)(2)). Subd. (o)(2) preserves requests to verify employment, landlord references and identity.
rules.effective_date_note: The current text was amended by SB 267 (Stats. 2023, ch. 776), effective January 1, 2024. The document does not say when the section's earlier provisions first took effect.
citation_aliases: Fair Employment and Housing Act (housing discrimination)
rules.quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.review_note: The section covers many protected classes. Only the source-of-income and screening-related parts are captured here.

rules.title: California FEHA housing discrimination: retaliatory eviction bar
rules.requirement: An owner may not harass, evict or otherwise discriminate against a person in the sale or rental of housing when the owner's dominant purpose is retaliation against a person who opposed unlawful housing practices, informed law enforcement of them, testified or assisted in a proceeding under the part, or aided others in exercising rights under the part. The provision does not delay an unlawful detainer action.

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of housing accommodations. The text states no unit-count or age limits.
coverage.other_conditions: Applies only where the owner's dominant purpose is retaliation for fair-housing-related activity.

rules.effective_date_note: The document states no separate effective date for subdivision (f). The section as amended took effect January 1, 2024.
rules.quoted_span: (f) For any owner of housing accommodations to harass, evict, or otherwise discriminate against any person in the sale or rental of housing accommodations when the owner’s dominant purpose is retaliation against a person who has opposed practices unlawful under this section, informed law enforcement agencies of practices believed unlawful under this section, has testified or assisted in any proceeding under this part, or has aided or encouraged a person to exercise or enjoy the rights secured by this part.
rules.review_note: This is a reprisal protection tied to eviction, not a just-cause eviction list. It is included under the category's reprisal-protection scope.

result.doc_summary: Official text of Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (FEHA housing discrimination), as amended by SB 267 effective January 1, 2024. It bars housing discrimination on many bases, including source of income (defined to include Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers). It sets screening rules for subsidized rentals on income standards and credit history, and bars retaliatory eviction for fair-housing activity. It states no deposit, fee, rent cap or algorithmic pricing rules.
